card.summary: Redis Free: 250 MB max data, 10 GB bandwidth/month, 1 database. Vector Free: 1 GB total data, 200M vectors x dims. QStash Free: 1,000 messages/day, 50 GB ban...

free_tier.stated: Redis Free: 250 MB max data, 10 GB bandwidth/month, 1 database. Vector Free: 1 GB total data, 200M vectors x dims. QStash Free: 1,000 messages/day, 50 GB bandwidth, 1 MB message.

retention.stated: Unclaimed ephemeral DBs deleted after 3 days.

egress.terms: Redis Free caps bandwidth at 10 GB/month with max data 250 MB. A 40x fetch amplification before the egress meter binds. Vector Free: bandwidth free/unmetered, storage 1 GB is the wall.

record.tooling: Redis protocol (any redis client), REST API for all three products, `@upstash/redis` SDK; QStash is HTTP-only
record.chaining: One free database per account on Redis Free ('Max databases | 1'). No per-project multiplication. BUT: `GET https://upstash.com/start-redis` mints a keyless, unauthenticated free Redis with no signup (deleted after 3 days unless claimed); claimed ones become normal free DBs. Vector's 1 GB with 1 MB per vector and 200M vectors is the better storage shape: unlimited vector COUNT, only total bytes capped.
record.limits_note: 250 MB is tiny. 1 database per account. QStash 1 MB max message size makes it useless as storage. Request size 10 MB (upgradeable). Unclaimed ephemeral DBs deleted after 3 days.
record.reliability_note: Ephemeral DBs (unclaimed) hard-delete at 3 days. Data vanishes by design. Claimed free DBs are durable.

card.summary: 250 MB max data size on Free; 500K commands per month; 10 GB bandwidth/month

free_tier.stated: 250 MB max data size on Free; 500K commands per month; 10 GB bandwidth/month

retention.stated: Free DBs minted anonymously are DELETED after 3 days unless claimed.

egress.terms: Free up to 10 GB per month on the Free plan (~333 MB per day), followed by metered bandwidth billing on paid tiers.

record.tooling: redis-cli over TLS, any Redis client, plus a body-style REST API (`POST` a JSON array command). Verified live: a free database can be minted with no signup via `POST https://upstash.com/start-redis` with an `Idempotency-Key` header.
record.chaining: Free tier is 1 database per account (pricing table: 'Max databases | 1'). 250 MB x N accounts. The command quota, not storage, is the wall: 500K commands/month = 16,667/day, and each GET returns at most 10 MB (verified), so max read throughput is 16,667 x 10 MB = 167 GB/day. 3x short of 500 GB/day even with a mythical 250 MB dataset read 667 times a day.
record.limits_note: 250 MB data; 10 MB max request size (LIVE-VERIFIED: a 20 MB SET returned 'ERR max request size exceeded. Limit: 10485760 bytes'); 100 MB max record size listed but the 10 MB request cap binds first; 10,000 max cmd/sec; 500K commands/month; 1 database
record.reliability_note: Works and is fast; the killer is the command meter. Every GET, SET, EXISTS, and even pipelined command counts. Operational commands (PING, AUTH, INFO, CONFIG, SELECT, COMMAND, RESET, QUIT) are explicitly not charged. Free DBs minted anonymously are DELETED after 3 days unless claimed.

evidence.proved: 'Free | $0/month | 250 MB | 10 GB' (Max Data / Max Bandwidth); FAQ: 'Free tier includes 250MB data size and 500K commands per month.'; 'Max databases | 1'
probe: POST (Idempotency-Key header) -> 200, credentials returned, 'Expires: 2026-10-24 (3 days from creation)'

probe: SET of a 1,000,000-byte value -> {"result":"OK"}; GET -> 1,000,013 bytes returned; STRLEN -> 1000000; 9 MB and 10,000,000-byte SETs also OK; a 20 MB SET -> {"error":"ERR max request size exceeded. Limit: 10485760 bytes"}

probe: INFO memory on the freshly minted free DB -> maxmemory:67108864 (64 MB), maxmemory_policy:noeviction — i.e. the anonymous/agent database is provisioned at 64 MB, well under the advertised 250 MB
arithmetic: 500,000 commands/month / 30 = 16,667 commands/day; x 10 MB max request = 167 GB/day ceiling. At a realistic 1 KB per command it is 16.7 MB/day — 30,000x short of 500 GB/day.

record.notes: 250 MB max data size on Free; 500K commands per month; 10 GB bandwidth/month

free_tier.stated: 1 GB total data+metadata on Free; 10K daily queries; 200M vectors x dimensions

egress.terms: Free (bandwidth price $0 on Free), but 1 GB of stored data makes it moot.

record.tooling: REST API, Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs; vectors are float arrays with up to 48 KB of metadata per vector, 1 MB max data per vector
record.chaining: 1 GB per database, 100 namespaces per index and 1 index on Free. Namespaces share the 1 GB, so they do not multiply. 500 GB needs 500 free accounts.
record.limits_note: 1 GB total; 10K queries/day (resets daily); 1 MB max per vector; 48 KB max metadata per vector; 1,536 max dimensions; 100 namespaces; 1 index
record.reliability_note: Stable managed service; queries are semantically searched rather than key-addressed, so it is a poor fit for blob retrieval anyway. You would use a 1-dimension vector as a pure key-value hack, which still hits the 1 GB cap.
